interface.title: Sentinel — Designer
interface.field: antibody engineering / protein biophysics (therapeutic antibody discovery)
interface.stage_of_work: pre-experimental triage — scoring and editing candidate sequences before committing wet-lab resources
interface.what_it_is_for: Paste or pick an antibody Fv (VH+VL) and get a CDR-aware liability scan, biophysical risk axes benchmarked against 1,093 clinical-stage antibodies, a 0–100 developability score, and ranked point mutations plus a one-click safe redesign that re-scores the combined variant.

data.note: A prebuilt library of 9 clinical antibodies (trastuzumab, adalimumab, bevacizumab, pembrolizumab, cetuximab, rituximab, omalizumab, infliximab, palivizumab) with 81 VH×VL pairings, a 1,093-antibody reference panel for percentiles, and jain2017.csv (n=136) for the validation tab. Live scoring of pasted sequences was exercised against the same-origin FastAPI backend (/api/analyze, /api/suggest, /api/redesign, /api/scan). I pasted trastuzumab's wild-type VH+VL by hand for the live-scoring run; data/candidates.csv was not reachable (404) and no upload control exists in this build.

features.name: Deep mutational scan grid
features.general: A position × variant heat grid that scores every possible single change at every sensitive position, with a hover readout of each cell's effect and a per-row 'best option' column, so a user can see where improvement headroom exists before editing anything
features.specific: Mutation map — every substitution at every CDR position, scored: rows are IMGT CDR positions across VH CDR1/2/3 and VL CDR1/2/3, columns are the 20 amino acids, cells are coloured worsens/neutral/improves with the wild-type residue outlined, and a 'best' column names the top substitution and its Δ composite score
steps: Produce a live report (paste VH+VL and press Analyze with a backend connected)
Press the 'Mutation map — deep mutational scan' disclosure to expand the grid
Read the legend (worsens / neutral / improves, outlined = wild-type) and the red/green field
Hover any cell for the exact call, e.g. 'N62→A (VH CDR2): +4'
Scan the 'best' column for positions that have a scoring substitution (e.g. D110E +4, W107A +0.5)
Scroll inside the grid to move from the VH CDRs down to the VL-kappa CDRs
serves_tasks: Scan every possible single change at every sensitive position to see where headroom exists
Get ranked single-change suggestions, each scored for benefit and for collateral risk

features.name: Mutation designer → safe redesign → before/after report toggle
features.general: A list of candidate single edits, each labelled safe or risky and annotated with its benefit and its side-effects, feeding a one-press 'apply the safe ones together' action that re-scores the combined result and lets the user flip between the original and the edited record
features.specific: Mutation designer cards (RECOMMENDED / CAUTION, Δscore, BLOSUM, binding-risk, guardrail counts, 'clears liability' vs 'partial') followed by the Redesign panel (strategy: safe) showing score → score, high-liab before → after, the applied substitution chips, which liabilities were cleared vs left for manual review, and the VH/VL strings with the changed residues highlighted; 'View redesigned report →' swaps the whole report to the variant and '← Back to original' returns
steps: Open a report that has flagged liabilities
Scroll to Mutation designer and compare the candidate fixes by Δscore and binding-risk — CDR3 edits are marked CAUTION / binding-risk high
Read the Redesign panel's combined result (e.g. 84 → 92, Δ+8, high-liab 2 → 1, 3 mutations) and which sites were deliberately left alone
Press 'View redesigned report →' to see the variant's own score, axes and shortened liability table
Press '← Back to original' to compare against the starting molecule
Repeat on another candidate (omalizumab: 44.3 → 53.9, high-liab 2 → 0)
serves_tasks: Get ranked single-change suggestions, each scored for benefit and for collateral risk
Apply the safe subset of changes together and compare before and after

features.name: VH × VL combination matrix with part pickers and leaderboard
features.general: Two checkbox lists of parts that define the rows and columns of a scored cross-product matrix; the matrix doubles as a picker — clicking a cell opens that combination's full record — and the same set is mirrored as a ranked, exportable shortlist underneath
features.specific: Combination explorer — mix VH × VL: tick/untick VH parts and VL parts (each labelled with its H3/L3 CDR3), read the 9×9 score matrix (native pairs outlined on the diagonal, colour from red through amber to green), hover to highlight a cell, click a cell for its chimera report, and use the Top combinations list (native/chimera tags) or its ⤓ CSV
steps: Open the Combination explorer tab
Untick parts in the VH and/or VL list to drop their row or column from the matrix
Read the colour-coded scores; native pairings are outlined on the diagonal
Click a cell to open that VH/VL chimera's full developability report (e.g. infliximab·VH / trastuzumab·VL, 90.9)
Scroll to Top combinations for the ranked shortlist, or click a row there to open the same report
Press ⤓ CSV for the leaderboard with per-axis values and red/amber/green flags
serves_tasks: Cross one set of parts against another and read the resulting grid of outcomes
Read the ranked shortlist and open any entry's full record
Export the whole ranking for downstream use

features.name: Shared design-criteria filter panel
features.general: A persistent sidebar of acceptance thresholds — two sliders and a set of must-pass checkboxes — that simultaneously gates two different views of the same collection: a card catalogue and a cross-product matrix, with a live count, an explicit empty state and a reset
features.specific: Design filters: 'Min developability score' slider, 'Max high-severity liabilities' slider, and 'Require green on…' checkboxes for the six axes; the Library header counts matches ('6 / 9 molecules') and the Combination explorer blanks every pairing that fails, down to 'No combinations pass the current filters'
steps: Drag 'Min developability score' up and watch the library count drop (9/9 → 7/9 at 61)
Drag 'Max high-severity liabilities' down to tighten further
Tick one or more 'Require green on…' axes (→ 6/9)
Switch to the Combination explorer — the same filters blank out failing cells and shorten the leaderboard and its CSV
Push a slider to its extreme to see the empty state
Press 'Reset filters' to restore the full set
serves_tasks: Narrow a set of items down to those that meet your acceptance criteria
Let the filters act on the cross-product view as well as the catalogue view

features.name: Scored risk report: traffic-light axes, radar, sited liability table, export
features.general: A single-item record that pairs a headline composite score and a plain-language verdict with several measured axes shown as green/amber/red against a reference population, the same axes as a radar outline, and a table of exactly where in the item each problem sits — all exportable as one file
features.specific: The Report view: composite /100 plus a Clean/Moderate/Elevated risk badge and a sentence naming the red flags, six developability axes with value · percentile vs the clinical set and a coloured dot (tooltips give each definition), a six-spoke radar, and a Sequence liabilities table of Sev / Type / Res / Site (IMGT, per chain) / Region with CDR1-3 badges; ⤓ CSV writes all of it out
steps: Open a report — from a library card, from a matrix cell, or by pasting VH+VL and pressing Analyze
Read the headline score, risk badge and the narrative naming the red flags
Scan the six axes for amber/red dots and their percentiles (omalizumab: charge asymmetry P92.1 red, Fv net charge P4.6 red)
Hover an axis label for its definition and the numbers behind it
Read the liability table to get the exact residue motif, IMGT site and CDR/framework region of each flag
Press ⤓ CSV to export score, axes and liabilities as one file
serves_tasks: Read the risk axes against a reference population and see which are out of range
List the exact problem sites found in the item, ranked by seriousness
Carry the result out of the tool as a file
Submit your own measurement for the same scoring

features.name: Predictor-vs-experiment correlation heatmap
features.general: A metric × measurement correlation grid that lets a user judge which computed quantity actually tracks which real assay, with the physically expected pairings outlined for reference and a plain-language 'best predictor for each measurement' summary underneath
features.specific: Validation vs experiment: Spearman ρ of each of the seven Sentinel axes against twelve measured assays (HIC, AC-SINS, PSR, Tm, SGAC-SINS, SMAC, CIC, CSI-BLI, BVP, ELISA, AccStab, HEK-Titer) over n=136 antibodies from jain2017.csv, red/white/green shaded, expected pairs outlined, plus a 'Best predictor per assay' list and a note on why rank correlation is used
steps: Open the Validation tab
Read the shaded ρ grid and its negative / ~0 / positive legend
Look for the outlined cells — the physically expected axis↔assay pairs (CDR hydrophobicity ↔ HIC, ρ=+0.375)
Compare a row across assays to see where an axis generalises and where it does not
Read 'Best predictor per assay' for the per-assay winner and its ρ
serves_tasks: Check how far the computed scores track real measurements before trusting them
